title: Nvidia’s board opens an independent investigation after CEO Jensen Huang admits an affair with a suspected Chinese spy
summary: Nvidia’s board announced Sunday, November 8, 2026, that a committee of independent directors, assisted by outside counsel, will investigate reports that CEO Jensen Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort. The board said it has “no reason to believe” national security or company secrets were compromised and that it has confidence in Huang and his leadership team. Nvidia also published a message in which Huang apologized for being unfaithful to his wife; a memo circulating among U.S. policymakers claims the woman, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, was recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security. Huang has committed to cooperating with the review, and the board set no timeline.

title: Wall Street futures edge up after a rough week, but Nvidia’s Huang probe unsettles investors
summary: Reuters reported Monday, November 9, 2026, that U.S. index futures attempted a recovery as investors hunted for bargains following last week’s steep slide. At 5:10 a.m. ET, S&P 500 E-minis were up 29.75 points, or 0.40%, Dow E-minis up 376 points, or 0.73%, and Nasdaq 100 E-minis up 56.5 points, or 0.21%. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index ended Friday with its biggest weekly loss since March 2025, and analysts said the gentler Nasdaq gains versus the Dow suggested investors remain selective. Of the 335 S&P 500 companies that had reported earnings as of Thursday, 82.4% beat estimates, according to LSEG.

title: Nvidia slides in premarket trading after its board opens an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang
summary: CNBC reported Monday, November 9, 2026, that Nvidia dropped nearly 5% in premarket trading after the company opened an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with a businesswoman whom U.S. intelligence agencies allege is a Chinese spy. Reuters put the premarket decline at 4.5% and described Nvidia as the second most valuable company in the world. CNBC noted that other semiconductor names held up comparatively well in early trading. A Capital.com analyst told Reuters that even speculation about leadership uncertainty could unsettle investors given Huang’s central role in the AI investment narrative.

title: AMD jumps in premarket after Oppenheimer upgrades the chipmaker to outperform with a $600 target
summary: CNBC reported Monday, November 9, 2026, that AMD shares advanced 3.2% in premarket trading after Oppenheimer upgraded the stock to outperform from market perform and set a price target of $600 per share. CNBC said that target implies 34% upside from Friday’s close. Analyst Rick Schafer turned bullish after AMD reported a strong third quarter last week, and the firm raised its estimates for future revenue and earnings per share. The move came as CNBC noted that most chip stocks held up well even as Nvidia fell.

title: SAP rises about 3% after JPMorgan upgrades it to Overweight, citing enterprise AI deployment
summary: Investing.com reported Monday, November 9, 2026, that SAP shares rose about 3% in premarket trading after JPMorgan upgraded the German software company to Overweight from Neutral. JPMorgan said enterprise AI is moving from experimentation to large-scale deployment and that growing corporate focus on data, controls and cost discipline strengthens incumbent platforms like SAP. The bank also said SAP’s own AI offering is improving and that further workforce transformation and AI-driven efficiencies could support margins. The note appeared in the same premarket roundup as Nvidia’s decline.

title: Anthropic reportedly buys $3.4 billion of gas-generator commitments to power its data centers
summary: The Financial Times reported Sunday, November 8, 2026, that Anthropic struck a roughly $3.4 billion deal for commitments covering 1.7 gigawatts of heavy-duty gas-fired generators from San Antonio-based OnePWR Solutions. The purchase was made in late September, and Anthropic did not acquire OnePWR itself or its employees, though the deal included engineering and construction capabilities to install the units. Reuters, relaying the report to CNBC, said it could not immediately verify it and that Anthropic and OnePWR did not respond to requests for comment. Reuters also noted its September report that Anthropic expects to spend more than $500 billion over ten years on AI infrastructure.

title: Trump tells ‘60 Minutes’ he “doesn’t mind guardrails” on AI and is open to working with Democrats
summary: Reuters reported Sunday, November 8, 2026, that President Donald Trump told CBS’s “60 Minutes” that AI risks can be managed but that he “doesn’t mind guardrails.” Asked whether the U.S. should accept AI’s risks to stay ahead of China, he signaled openness to working with Democrats on safeguards. He added that he did not want regulation to leave the United States in “a deep second position” behind China, which he said has no such restrictions. Reuters noted Trump has previously favored letting tech companies police themselves, and that it remains unclear what level of safeguards he would accept.

title: DeepSeek says its Harness agent app hit 1.54 million daily users, consuming about 92 trillion tokens a day
summary: Bloomberg, via The Business Times, reported Monday, November 9, 2026, that DeepSeek disclosed on X that its open-source agent app Harness reached 1.54 million daily active users by November 4, less than three months after its August 13 debut. Daily users were about 271,000 at the end of September. The app consumes roughly 92 trillion tokens a day, about 60 million per active user, an early sign of how much more compute agents need than chatbots. DeepSeek counts about 35,000 plug-ins, says 60% of users have built at least one, and plans an official plug-in marketplace with a support program for creators.

title: Report: Apple’s Ternus pushes Federighi to speed up Siri and make it more agentic
summary: The Verge reported Sunday, November 8, 2026, citing Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, that Apple CEO John Ternus is pressing AI chief Craig Federighi to accelerate the Siri roadmap and deliver a powerful agent that can compete with OpenAI’s Dots or Meta’s Muse. Fine-grained control of Apple’s own apps is expected with iOS 27.3, while third-party app integration is likely to arrive in the spring, per Gurman. He believes Apple could make Siri more agent-like as early as next year, able to keep pursuing goals without the user prompting each step. These are reported plans and expectations, not announced products.

title: Elvis and Eminem rights holders sue AI music company Suno over voice and lyric clones
summary: The Verge reported Sunday, November 8, 2026, that rights holders of Elvis Presley’s music and the publisher of some of Eminem’s biggest records are suing Suno, claiming it illegally generates music and lyrics that mimic those artists. The Presley suit invokes Tennessee’s ELVIS Act, which makes it illegal for an AI company to clone a singer’s voice. A Suno spokesperson said the company does not allow prompts for specific artists’ names and songs and works with third-party providers to screen uploaded audio and lyrics for misuse. The suits add to cases already brought by Sony, UMG, Jason Isbell, Reservoir Media and others.

title: Deep Principle releases Hydrogen-1.0, an open-weight model for chemistry and materials research
summary: In a November 6, 2026 release, Deep Principle said it introduced Hydrogen-1.0 on November 4, an open-weight scientific model built by post-training GLM-5.3 on chemistry, materials and life-science data plus records from its own laboratories. It is meant to help teams plan experiments, run computational workflows and explore candidate materials. In the company’s own evaluations, it reached a mean best-so-far HOMO–LUMO gap of 4.318 eV in a five-round complex-design test versus 3.689 eV for GPT-6-Astra and 3.353 eV for Kimi-K3. Weights are on Hugging Face and ModelScope, with API access on NeuroSpark and use inside Deep Principle’s Mira AI Scientist.

title: Alibaba’s Co-Design Bench finds the best coding agent fully completes only 26.4% of real-world tasks
summary: The Decoder reported November 8, 2026, that researchers from Alibaba and several Asian universities built Co-Design Bench from real user change requests that had already tripped up agents. GPT-6 Astra, the best of ten models tested, meets about 70% of a task’s requirements on average but is fully correct on only 26.4% of tasks. Claude Opus 5 and Qwen3.8-Max followed, with Grok 4.6 last. Older benchmarks show scores above 99%, and the study found results also depend on the harness an agent runs in. The authors note limits, including one fixed request per task and possible mistakes by AI judges.

title: MIT’s WorldParticle uses one AI model to simulate sand, fluids and folding proteins
summary: MIT News reported November 9, 2026, that researchers at MIT, the University of British Columbia and elsewhere built WorldParticle, a single deep-learning system that represents materials as tiny particles and predicts where they move one step at a time. It replaces separate hand-coded simulators for different physical phenomena. The team demonstrated it on six phenomena, including deformable objects, granular materials and proteins, with higher accuracy than numerical simulation methods. It modeled protein structure changes about 100 times faster than numerical simulators, and the work will be presented at ACM SIGGRAPH Asia.

title: Hands-on: NYT Cooking’s AI assistant rescues a weeknight chicken dinner but nearly ruins a cake
summary: The Verge’s Jennifer Pattison Tuohy reported November 7, 2026, after testing the new AI assistant in NYT Cooking, available to subscribers on iOS at launch. It rewrites a recipe for ingredient swaps, scaling or missing equipment, highlights every change in a “Your Version” tab, and leaves the original untouched. In her tests it turned a chicken-and-rice recipe into a new version using green beans and suggested converting a Bundt cake into muffins. But it once used a modified six-tablespoon butter amount without saying which version it meant, instead of the original three-quarter cup, so she advises double-checking amounts and times.

title: WIRED explains how world models are training robots and self-driving cars in simulation
summary: WIRED reported November 8, 2026, that world models take a visual state of the world and predict the next one, generating physics-aware 3D simulations. Niantic Spatial, which came from Pokémon Go, wants to use its scan data to build replicas where robots can run “millions of simulations,” while Wayve uses dashcam footage to recreate hazardous roads that would be impractical to test for real. The piece says 2027 could be a major year for home robots and driverless cars, and notes that AI labs need people to record real life, creating new gig work.

title: McGill students build Silent Voice to let cancer patients speak again in their own cloned voice
summary: HeadTopics, compiling CTV Toronto and CP24 reporting published November 7–8, 2026, said four third-year McGill University students built Silent Voice in 36 hours at Cal Hacks and placed second overall. Users who lost their voice box wear face sensors and mouth words, and the system plays them back in a clone of their own voice, which can be made from as little as a 30-second video. Each electrode costs about $20, and the students want to keep it affordable and eventually reduce reliance on electrodes, perhaps using a phone camera. It remains a student prototype that they hope to fund and turn into an app.

title: Kenyan innovator’s recycled-plastic robots are translating STEM lessons into sign language for deaf students
summary: The Aspire Institute reported November 5, 2026, on Norah Kimathi, whose Zerobionic project began as a robotic hand made from recycled plastic and grew into AI-powered humanoid robots that translate science concepts into sign language. Teachers can program standardized signs for lessons, and pilot projects showed STEM comprehension improvements of up to 70 percent. By 2025 the technology had reached more than 510,000 students and over 8,000 teachers, and it has repurposed more than 10,000 kilograms of plastic waste. Kimathi says her seed-fund prototype achieved real-time speech-to-sign translation with under two seconds of latency and 92 percent accuracy.

title: Blue Monday Allstars and the Bayou Blues Band play The Ruins tonight
summary: The Blue Monday Concert Series continues tonight, Monday, November 9, 2026, at The Ruins, 1919 Kaliste Saloom Rd., Suite 303, Lafayette. The Love of People listing features the Blue Monday Allstars with special guest The Bayou Blues Band. Doors open at 5 p.m., with music and food served at 6 p.m. General admission was listed at $20 plus a $0.50 service fee and includes a blue plate special of red beans and rice while supplies last. The listing shows online ticket sales have ended, so check with the organizers about availability at the door.

title: Lafayette Public Library’s Makerspace offers a Cajun Recipe Box grab-and-go kit Tuesday
summary: On Tuesday, November 10, 2026, from 1:00 to 7:30 p.m., the Main Library Makerspace at 301 W. Congress St. in Lafayette offers its November Grab & Go kit: assemble a recipe box with South Louisiana flair using laser-cut wooden parts. The library’s listing says kits include most of the supplies needed plus instructions. They are for ages 13 and up, available during Makerspace Open Access hours only, while supplies last.

title: Aaron Lewis brings his Acoustic Origins Tour to the Cajundome Convention Center Wednesday
summary: Aaron Lewis: The Acoustic Origins Tour comes to the Cajundome Convention Center, 444 Cajundome Blvd., Lafayette, on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, with doors at 6 p.m. and the show at 7 p.m. The Cajundome listing says tickets are on sale through Ticketmaster and that everyone needs a ticket, including SafeTix mobile tickets. The venue also notes a clear bag policy and a cashless payment system at concessions and merchandise stands. Free parking is listed at Congress Street Gate 8.

title: Paul Thorn Band plays ‘Life Is Just A Vapor’ at Acadiana Center for the Arts Thursday
summary: The Paul Thorn Band performs Thursday, November 12, 2026, from 7:30 to 9:45 p.m. in the James Devin Moncus Theater at the Acadiana Center for the Arts, 101 W. Vermilion St., Lafayette. The AcA listing says his new album, Life Is Just A Vapor, is packed with short, wise lines like “tough times don’t last, but tough people do.” It describes Thorn as a storyteller who balances humor and pathos, and notes the box office opens one hour before showtime.

title: Second Saturday ArtWalk fills Downtown Lafayette with galleries, music and performances
summary: Downtown Lafayette’s November ArtWalk runs Saturday, November 14, 2026, from 5 to 9 p.m. According to Downtown Lafayette, museums, independent galleries, studios, craft stores and art houses in the cultural district take part, each hosting its own events with local artists and performers. ArtWalk happens every second Saturday, rain or shine. The listing notes metered street parking is free after 5 p.m. on weekdays and all day on weekends, and the Parc-Auto du Centre-Ville garage at 121 E. Vermilion St. has 530 spaces.
